_about: Public-domain Jan Hus (c. 1369-1415), the Bohemian reformer burned at Constance, for the Word Hoard: his Letters written during his exile and imprisonment, with Luther's preface (Edinburgh, 1846); The Letters of John Hus, edited by Herbert B. Workman and R. Martin Pope (1904); De Ecclesia, The Church, translated by David S. Schaff (1915); and the Latin Tractatus Responsivus, edited by S. Harrison Thomson (Princeton, 1927). Texts are from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 81 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

hus-letters-1846: Letters of John Huss written during his exile and imprisonment (Edinburgh, W. Whyte, 1846)
hus-letters-workman-pope: The Letters of John Hus (London : Hodder and Stoughton, 1904)
hus-de-ecclesia-schaff: De ecclesia. The Church (New York Scribner, 1915)
hus-tractatus-responsivus: Mag. Johannis Hus Tractatus responsivus : now first edited with a critical introduction and notes from the unique ms. cod. C. 116, Metropolitan chapter library, Prague (Princeton : Princeton university press, 1927)

_excluded.hus-czech: the Czech collected works (Sebrané spisy) and Czech correspondence, left for a lane that takes Czech

_pending.hus-latin-sentences: Super IV Sententiarum (Flajshans, 1904-1906): its IA volumes still need matching
